about: English-language text sources where English speakers in Israel and the Orthodox English-speaking world use Hebrew words inside English. Read by the anglo-usage and news-vocab skills. Text is mined for terms, spellings and usage patterns only; source text is never copied into the bank (posts and articles are copyrighted by their authors, and the bank feeds public datasets).
verified_how: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' on each feed from an Israeli residential IP; status and <item> count recorded. Article routes are from news-vocab (2026-10-19) unless stated.

registers.news: Israeli English news: names, places, institutions, Hebrew loan words in coverage
registers.opinion: first-person anglo voice: aliyah, army, bureaucracy, family life
registers.frum_news: Orthodox / Haredi English news: yeshivish and Ashkenazi forms (Shabbos, shlita, bochur)
registers.torah: weekly parsha and holiday content: parsha names, Torah vocabulary
registers.community: local anglo noticeboards and lists: errands, simchas, services, neighbourhood life

sources.name: Times of Israel (news)
sources.articles: WebFetch (curl gets 403 from Cloudflare on articles)

sources.name: Times of Israel Blogs
sources.articles: WebFetch (confirmed 2026-10-23). WebFetch returns a small-model summary, so spellings in it are less reliable than a raw read.
sources.notes: Best single source for the first-person anglo voice. https://www.timesofisrael.com/blogs/feed/ is an empty channel (200, 0 items): use the blogs. subdomain.
sources.yield_2026_10_23: About 10 items per feed page (use ?paged=2, ?paged=3), all from the last day; mostly parsha essays and election pieces. Writers use Israeli/academic forms (Bereishit, Avraham, Shabbat, parasha/sedra). Nothing on simchas, mourning, mikveh or the Rabbanut that day.

sources.name: Times of Israel, Jewish Times section
sources.yield_2026_10_23: Diaspora and antisemitism news, no first-person anglo writing. Poor for usage.

sources.name: Times of Israel, Israel Inside section
sources.yield_2026_10_23: News and election coverage; low value for everyday religious usage.

sources.name: Jerusalem Post (front page)
sources.articles: curl with a browser user agent; text in the JSON-LD "articleBody"

sources.name: Jerusalem Post, Judaism
sources.articles: curl with a browser user agent, JSON-LD "articleBody" (confirmed 2026-10-23; Torah-portion columns live under /judaism/torah-portion/)
sources.yield_2026_10_23: Weekly parsha and haftarah columns, Israeli forms throughout (Parashat, Bereishit, Simchat Torah). Good for parsha-as-content patterns.

sources.name: Jerusalem Post, Diaspora (the Jewish World section)
sources.feed_status: listed on https://www.jpost.com/rss on 2026-10-23; not fetched
sources.notes: https://www.jpost.com/rss/rssfeedsjewishworld.aspx and .../rssfeedsjewishworldnews return 404. The index page https://www.jpost.com/rss lists every current feed.

sources.name: Yeshiva World News
sources.yield_2026_10_23: RSS descriptions are short teasers; items that day were politics and news. Low yield for simcha and lifestyle words.

sources.name: VINnews
sources.yield_2026_10_23: Mostly general and Israeli news; Hebrew-script honorifics in death notices.

sources.name: Matzav
sources.articles: article pages are client-rendered shells (one extracted six words); use the feed's content:encoded instead (2026-10-23)
sources.yield_2026_10_23: Richest for chareidi politics vocabulary (yeshivos, gedolim, Moetzes, kol korei).

sources.name: Israel National News (Arutz Sheva)
sources.notes: Religious-Zionist register: Sephardi/Israeli forms (Shabbat, Bereshit) beside Hebrew place names in Judea and Samaria.
sources.yield_2026_10_23: The feed is news flashes only; no Torah content. Low value for this register.

sources.name: Chabad.org, weekly parsha
sources.feed_status: 200, 30 items (this week's parsha: Nutshell, Text, Rashi, In Depth, Chassidic Masters)
sources.articles: curl gets 403 on article and parshah pages; WebFetch works (2026-10-23)
sources.notes: Daniel, 2026-10-23: chabad.org for Ashkenazi pronunciation. Chabad spells parshas, holidays and terms the Ashkenazi way. The feed only has the current week, so one run covers one parsha; for the full cycle walk https://www.chabad.org/parshah/ instead. https://www.chabad.org/news/rss.xml returns 403.
sources.yield_2026_10_23: Parshah/Parshat with -ah endings, but Shabbat rather than Shabbos on the page read: Chabad's site is not consistently Ashkenazi. Frum news (COLlive, Anash) is the more reliable Ashkenazi source.

sources.name: COLlive (Chabad community news)
sources.yield_2026_10_23: Best for yeshiva and Chabad usage (bochur, Rebbeim, shliach, Shiur Alef). Wedding posts are photos with no text.

sources.name: Anash.org
sources.yield_2026_10_23: Best for Chabad community vocabulary (engagement notices with the l'chaim, mikveh funding, halacha columns on plag hamincha and bein hashmashos).

sources.name: Aish.com
sources.articles: curl works (200); the body sits inside full-page HTML, so strip scripts and navigation (2026-10-23)
sources.yield_2026_10_23: Parsha essays titled with the parsha plus a theme; neutral forms (parsha, Shabbat).

sources.name: Janglo
sources.articles: not yet tried; probably needs Claude in Chrome
sources.notes: Classifieds and community board for anglos in Israel. Posts are by private individuals: take usage patterns only, never names or details.

yield_note: On the first run (2026-10-23) the news feeds carried almost none of the simcha and lifestyle words (shlita, heimish, sheitel, tichel, aufruf, bentch, sheva brachos, vort, shtender, bekeshe, kiddush levana). Writers used their own knowledge for those, and the pack note says so. Better places for them: simcha and lifestyle sections, community notices, classifieds.
